theory.title: Repaso integrado: cambios, arrepentimientos, planes y acción comunitaria
theory.explanation: Este punto de control repasa los contenidos de la Unidad 5 y no introduce gramática nueva. Combina comparativos de cambio, futuro continuo, tercer condicional, arrepentimientos con wish, expresiones de cantidad, verbos para transmitir mensajes, conectores de concesión y resultado, tendencias presentes y futuro perfecto.
theory.tip: Escoge el tiempo verbal según si describes una tendencia, una acción futura en curso, un resultado pasado imaginario o una meta completada.

content.passage: The neighbourhood has become more environmentally aware. More and more residents are cycling, and the number of people using reusable bags is increasing. Last year, the council launched a campaign. If it had started earlier, it would have reached more families. Some residents wish they had joined the first clean-up day. By 2030, the council will have planted thousands of trees. Despite the challenges, the community is making steady progress.

items.prompt: Summarise an environmental change using comparative structures.
items.modelAnswer: Our town has become greener because the council has planted trees and improved the recycling service. More residents are using reusable bags, and the new cycle route has made short journeys safer. There is still more work to do.

items.prompt: Describe what volunteers will be doing next year.
items.modelAnswer: Next year, volunteers will be organising monthly clean-ups, helping at the community garden and teaching children about local wildlife. Some will be collecting donations, while others will be repairing equipment.

items.prompt: Explain what might have happened if a campaign had started earlier.
items.modelAnswer: If the campaign had started earlier, more shops might have reduced their plastic packaging before the summer festival. We could have avoided a large amount of waste. It shows why planning and communication matter.

items.prompt: Talk about a past action you wish you had taken.
items.modelAnswer: I wish I had joined the local river clean-up last year. I had time, but I didn't realise how much rubbish had collected there. I have learned to look for community events and take part when I can.

items.prompt: Describe a project supported by a large number of people.
items.modelAnswer: The neighbourhood food project has plenty of support from residents, schools and local shops. People donate food, sort boxes and deliver them to families. The project works because many people contribute in small ways.

items.prompt: Give advice using a reporting verb.
items.modelAnswer: The organiser advised volunteers to wear gloves, reminded them to bring water and warned them not to enter the river. She also told everyone to report dangerous objects. The instructions helped the event run safely.

items.prompt: Present an argument with a concession and a result.
items.modelAnswer: Although improving public transport can be expensive, it can reduce traffic and pollution. The council should start with the busiest routes; therefore, more people will notice the benefits and may leave their cars at home.

items.prompt: Describe a trend happening in your area.
items.modelAnswer: More residents are cycling to work and using refillable bottles. Local shops are also offering products with less packaging. These trends suggest that environmental choices are becoming part of everyday life.

items.prompt: Predict what your town will have achieved by 2030.
items.modelAnswer: By 2030, our town will have improved its cycle network and planted more trees in public spaces. It will also have introduced better recycling points. I hope residents will have helped shape these plans.

items.prompt: Review the most useful language from this unit.
items.modelAnswer: This unit has helped me compare changes, discuss environmental projects and make predictions about the future. I've practised explaining regrets and giving advice. I can now describe community action and its possible results more clearly.

A: The organisers have received a lot of support and hope to continue the project in the future.
